units: Absolute USD; shares and vessel-days in units; EPS in USD/share

normalization_policy.ebit: No unsupported operating addbacks. Retain G&A, employee compensation, SBC if embedded, voyage costs, and cyclical freight results.
normalization_policy.net_income: Reported NI minus unrealized derivative gains, plus debt-extinguishment losses, minus loan-modification gains. Retain realized hedging, FX, recurring financing amortization and operating expenses. No tax adjustment because the reported statements contain no income tax line; tonnage taxes remain operating expenses.
normalization_policy.cfo: Keep actual reported CFO, after cash interest and working capital. Noncash adjustments already included in CFO are never added again.
normalization_policy.fcf: Actual levered post-investment cash = reported CFO minus cash paid for vessel acquisitions/advances minus special survey/drydocking. Does not subtract principal repayments, which are financing; does not add equity/debt proceeds. Interest receipts are investing and shown separately.
normalization_policy.ttm: Additive flow amounts = FY minus H1 prior plus H1 current. TTM EPS is NI divided by day-weighted average shares, not a subtraction or sum of reported EPS.
normalization_policy.sbc: A missing separate amount remains null; no SBC addback.

warnings: Quarterly and interim releases are unaudited; annual audited figures take precedence.
Rounded operating-day totals can differ by one day across the annual/quarterly bridge. Preserve reported daily TCE and derived daily TCE separately.
Reported EPS is taken directly from each original quarter. No annual EPS less nine-month EPS. Derived TTM EPS is explicitly not reported EPS.
No separate SBC amount established; no SBC addback.
Historical normalized EBIT still includes peak freight earnings. These are operating results, not exceptional accounting gains. Use an independent through-cycle valuation scenario.
Cash after disclosed drydock is not sustainable owner earnings: fleet replacement is not fully represented by drydock spending.
Sale-and-leaseback repurchases repay an existing financing liability; do not count them again as fleet capex.
